ayahs.textArabic: الٓرۚ تِلۡكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ ٱلۡمُبِينِ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Alif-Laaam-Raa; tilka Aayaatul Kitaabil Mubeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Alif-Lãm-Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book.

ayahs.textArabic: إِنَّآ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ قُرۡءَٰنًا عَرَبِيّٗا لَّعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Innaaa anzalnaahu quraanan 'Arabiyyal la-'allakum ta'qiloon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Quran so that you may understand.

ayahs.textArabic: نَحۡنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ أَحۡسَنَ ٱلۡقَصَصِ بِمَآ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ وَإِن كُنتَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلۡغَٰفِلِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Nahnu naqussu 'alaika ahsanal qasasi bimaaa awhainaaa ilaika haazal quraana Wa-in kunta min qablihee laminal ghaafileen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: We relate to you, [O Muhammad], the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an although you were, before it, among the unaware.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: We relate to you ˹O Prophet˺ the best of stories through Our revelation of this Quran, though before this you were totally unaware ˹of them˺.

ayahs.textArabic: إِذۡ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّي رَأَيۡتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوۡكَبٗا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ رَأَيۡتُهُمۡ لِي سَٰجِدِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Iz qaala Yoosufu li-abeehi yaaa-abati innee ra-aytu ahada 'ashara kawkabanw wash-shamsa walqamara ra-aytuhum lee saajideen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: [Of these stories mention] when Joseph said to his father, "O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: ˹Remember˺ when Joseph said to his father, “O my dear father! Indeed I dreamt of eleven stars, and the sun, and the moon—I saw them prostrating to me!”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ لَا تَقۡصُصۡ رُءۡيَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ إِخۡوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُواْ لَكَ كَيۡدًاۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ عَدُوّٞ مُّبِينٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala yaa-bunaiya laa taqsus ru'yaaka 'alaaa ikhwatika fayakeedoo laka kaidaa; innash Shaitaana lil-insaani 'aduwwum mubeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: He said, "O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers or they will contrive against you a plan. Indeed Satan, to man, is a manifest enemy.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: He replied, “O my dear son! Do not relate your vision to your brothers, or they will devise a plot against you. Surely Satan is a sworn enemy to humankind.

ayahs.textArabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَجۡتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِن تَأۡوِيلِ ٱلۡأَحَادِيثِ وَيُتِمُّ نِعۡمَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ ءَالِ يَعۡقُوبَ كَمَآ أَتَمَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَبَوَيۡكَ مِن قَبۡلُ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-kazaalika yajtabeeka rabbuka Wa-yu'allimuka min ta'weelil ahaadeesi Wa-yutimmu ni'matahoo 'alaika Wa-'alaaa Aali Ya'qooba kamaaa atammahaa 'alaaa abawaika min qablu Ibraaheema Wa-Ishaaq; inna Rabbaka 'Aleemun hakeem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And so will your Lord choose you ˹O Joseph˺, and teach you the interpretation of dreams, and perfect His favour upon you and the descendants of Jacob—˹just˺ as He once perfected it upon your forefathers, Abraham and Isaac. Surely your Lord is All-Knowing, All-Wise.”

ayahs.textArabic: ۞ لَّقَدۡ كَانَ فِي يُوسُفَ وَإِخۡوَتِهِۦٓ ءَايَٰتٞ لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Laqad kaana fee Yoosufa Wa-ikhwatiheee Aayaatul lissaaa'ileen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Certainly were there in Joseph and his brothers signs for those who ask,
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Indeed, in the story of Joseph and his brothers there are lessons for all who ask.

ayahs.textArabic: إِذۡ قَالُواْ لَيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِينَا مِنَّا وَنَحۡنُ عُصۡبَةٌ إِنَّ أَبَانَا لَفِي ضَلَٰلٖ مُّبِينٍ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Iz qaaloo la-Yoosufu Wa-akhoohu ahabbu ilaaa Abeenaa minnaa Wa-nahnu 'usbatun; inna abaanaa lafee dalaalim mubeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: When they said, "Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a clan. Indeed, our father is in clear error.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: ˹Remember˺ when they said ˹to one another˺, “Surely Joseph and his brother ˹Benjamin˺ are more beloved to our father than we, even though we are a group of so many. Indeed, our father is clearly mistaken.

ayahs.textArabic: ٱقۡتُلُواْ يُوسُفَ أَوِ ٱطۡرَحُوهُ أَرۡضٗا يَخۡلُ لَكُمۡ وَجۡهُ أَبِيكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ قَوۡمٗا صَٰلِحِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Uqtuloo Yoosufa awitra hoohu ardany yakhlu lakum wajhu abeekum Wa-takoonoo mim ba'dihee qawman saaliheen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Kill Joseph or cast him out to [another] land; the countenance of your father will [then] be only for you, and you will be after that a righteous people."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Kill Joseph or cast him out to some ˹distant˺ land so that our father’s attention will be only ours, then after that you may ˹repent and˺ become righteous people!”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ قَآئِلٞ مِّنۡهُمۡ لَا تَقۡتُلُواْ يُوسُفَ وَأَلۡقُوهُ فِي غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلۡجُبِّ يَلۡتَقِطۡهُ بَعۡضُ ٱلسَّيَّارَةِ إِن كُنتُمۡ فَٰعِلِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaalaa qaaa'ilum minhum laa taqtuloo Yoosufa Wa-alqoohu fee ghayaabatil jubbi yaltaqithu badus sai-yaarati in kuntum faa-'ileen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Said a speaker among them, "Do not kill Joseph but throw him into the bottom of the well; some travelers will pick him up - if you would do [something]."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: One of them said, “Do not kill Joseph. But if you must do something, throw him into the bottom of a well so perhaps he may be picked up by some travellers.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مَا لَكَ لَا تَأۡمَ۬نَّا عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَنَٰصِحُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo yaaa-abaanaa maa laka laa ta'mannaa 'alaa Yoosufa Wa-innaa lahoo lanaa-sihoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "O our father, why do you not entrust us with Joseph while indeed, we are to him sincere counselors?
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They said, “O our father! Why do you not trust us with Joseph, although we truly wish him well?

ayahs.textArabic: أَرۡسِلۡهُ مَعَنَا غَدٗا يَرۡتَعۡ وَيَلۡعَبۡ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Arsillhu ma'anaa ghadany yarta'wa yal'ab Wa-innaa lahoo lahaafizoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Send him with us tomorrow that he may eat well and play. And indeed, we will be his guardians.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Send him out with us tomorrow so that he may enjoy himself and play. And we will really watch over him.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ إِنِّي لَيَحۡزُنُنِيٓ أَن تَذۡهَبُواْ بِهِۦ وَأَخَافُ أَن يَأۡكُلَهُ ٱلذِّئۡبُ وَأَنتُمۡ عَنۡهُ غَٰفِلُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala innee la-yahzununeee an tazhaboo bihee Wa-akhaafu any ya'kulahuz zi'bu Wa-antum 'anhu ghaafiloon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: [Jacob] said, "Indeed, it saddens me that you should take him, and I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are of him unaware."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: He responded, “It would truly sadden me if you took him away with you, and I fear that a wolf may devour him while you are negligent of him.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ لَئِنۡ أَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئۡبُ وَنَحۡنُ عُصۡبَةٌ إِنَّآ إِذٗا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo la-in akalahuz zi'bu Wa-nahnu 'usbatun innaaa izal lakhaasiroon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "If a wolf should eat him while we are a [strong] clan, indeed, we would then be losers."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They said, “If a wolf were to devour him, despite our strong group, then we would certainly be losers!”

ayahs.textArabic: فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُواْ بِهِۦ وَأَجۡمَعُوٓاْ أَن يَجۡعَلُوهُ فِي غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلۡجُبِّۚ وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡهِ لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهُم بِأَمۡرِهِمۡ هَٰذَا وَهُمۡ لَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Falammaa zahaboo bihee Wa-ajma'ooo aien yaj'aloohu fee ghayaabatil jubb; Wa-awhainaaa ilaihi latunabbi-'annahum bi-amrihim haaza Wa-hum laa yash'uroon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: So when they took him [out] and agreed to put him into the bottom of the well... But We inspired to him, "You will surely inform them [someday] about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive [your identity]."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And so, when they took him away and decided to throw him into the bottom of the well, We inspired him: “˹One day˺ you will remind them of this deed of theirs while they are unaware ˹of who you are˺.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَجَآءُوٓ أَبَاهُمۡ عِشَآءٗ يَبۡكُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-jaaa'ooo abaahum 'ishaaa-'aien yabkoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And they came to their father at night, weeping.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Then they returned to their father in the evening, weeping.

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ يَٰٓأَبَانَآ إِنَّا ذَهَبۡنَا نَسۡتَبِقُ وَتَرَكۡنَا يُوسُفَ عِندَ مَتَٰعِنَا فَأَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئۡبُۖ وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤۡمِنٖ لَّنَا وَلَوۡ كُنَّا صَٰدِقِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo yaaa-abaanaaa innaa zahabnaa nastabiqu Wa-taraknaa Yoosufa 'inda mataa'inaa fa-akhalahuz zi'b, Wa-maaa anta bimu'minil lanaa Wa-law kunnaa saadiqeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "O our father, indeed we went racing each other and left Joseph with our possessions, and a wolf ate him. But you would not believe us, even if we were truthful."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They cried, “Our father! We went racing and left Joseph with our belongings, and a wolf devoured him! But you will not believe us, no matter how truthful we are.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَجَآءُو عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِۦ بِدَمٖ كَذِبٖۚ قَالَ بَلۡ سَوَّلَتۡ لَكُمۡ أَنفُسُكُمۡ أَمۡرٗاۖ فَصَبۡرٞ جَمِيلٞۖ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُسۡتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-jaaa'oo 'alaa qameesi-hee bidamin kazib qaala bal sawwalat lakum anfusukum amraa; fasabrun jameel; wallaahul musta'aanu 'alaa maa tasifoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And they brought upon his shirt false blood. [Jacob] said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help against that which you describe."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And they brought his shirt, stained with false blood. He responded, “No! Your souls must have tempted you to do something ˹evil˺. So ˹I can only endure with˺ beautiful patience! It is Allah’s help that I seek to bear your claims.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَجَآءَتۡ سَيَّارَةٞ فَأَرۡسَلُواْ وَارِدَهُمۡ فَأَدۡلَىٰ دَلۡوَهُۥۖ قَالَ يَٰبُشۡرَىٰ هَٰذَا غُلَٰمٞۚ وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَٰعَةٗۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِمَا يَعۡمَلُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-jaaa'at saiyyaaratun fa-arsaloo waaridahum fa-adlaa dalwah; qaala yaa-bushraa haaza ghulaam; Wa-asarroohu bi-daa'ah; wallaahu 'aleemum bimaa ya'maloon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And there came a company of travelers; then they sent their water drawer, and he let down his bucket. He said, "Good news! Here is a boy." And they concealed him, [taking him] as merchandise; and Allah was knowing of what they did.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And there came some travellers, and they sent their water-boy who let down his bucket into the well. He cried out, “Oh, what a great find! Here is a boy!” And they took him secretly ˹to be sold˺ as merchandise, but Allah is All-Knowing of what they did.

ayahs.textArabic: وَشَرَوۡهُ بِثَمَنِۭ بَخۡسٖ دَرَٰهِمَ مَعۡدُودَةٖ وَكَانُواْ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلزَّٰهِدِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-sharawhu bisamanim bakhsin daraahima ma'doo-datinw Wa-kaanoo feehi minaz zaahideen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And they sold him for a reduced price - a few dirhams - and they were, concerning him, of those content with little.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They ˹later˺ sold him for a cheap price, just a few silver coins—only wanting to get rid of him.

ayahs.textArabic: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِي ٱشۡتَرَىٰهُ مِن مِّصۡرَ لِٱمۡرَأَتِهِۦٓ أَكۡرِمِي مَثۡوَىٰهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوۡ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدٗاۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُۥ مِن تَأۡوِيلِ ٱلۡأَحَادِيثِۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡرِهِۦ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-qaalal lazish taraahu mim Misra limra atiheee akrimee maswaahu 'asaaa any-yanfa'anaaa aw nattakhizahoo waladaa; Wa-kazaalika mak-kannaa li-Yoosufa fil ardi Wa-linu'allimahoo min ta'weelil ahaadees; wallaahu ghaalibun 'alaaa amrihee Wa-laakinna aksaran naasi laa ya'lamoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And the one from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, "Make his residence comfortable. Perhaps he will benefit us, or we will adopt him as a son." And thus, We established Joseph in the land that We might teach him the interpretation of events. And Allah is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: The man from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, “Take good care of him, perhaps he may be useful to us or we may adopt him as a son.” This is how We established Joseph in the land, so that We might teach him the interpretation of dreams. Allah’s Will always prevails, but most people do not know.

ayahs.textArabic: وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥٓ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ حُكۡمٗا وَعِلۡمٗاۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-lammaa balagha ashuddahooo aatainaahu hukmanw Wa-'ilmaa; Wa-kazaa-lika najzil muhsineen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And when Joseph reached maturity, We gave him judgment and knowledge. And thus We reward the doers of good.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And when he reached maturity, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. This is how We reward the good-doers.

ayahs.textArabic: وَرَٰوَدَتۡهُ ٱلَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيۡتِهَا عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦ وَغَلَّقَتِ ٱلۡأَبۡوَٰبَ وَقَالَتۡ هَيۡتَ لَكَۚ قَالَ مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهُۥ رَبِّيٓ أَحۡسَنَ مَثۡوَايَۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-raawadat-hul latee huwa fee baitihaa 'an nafsihee Wa-ghallaqatil abwaaba Wa-qaalat haita lak; qaala ma'aazal laahi innahoo rabbeee ahsana maswaay; innahoo laa yuflihuz zaalimoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, "Come, you." He said, "[I seek] the refuge of Allah. Indeed, he is my master, who has made good my residence. Indeed, wrongdoers will not succeed."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And the lady, in whose house he lived, tried to seduce him. She locked the doors ˹firmly˺ and said, “Come to me!” He replied, “Allah is my refuge! It is ˹not right to betray˺ my master, who has taken good care of me. Indeed, the wrongdoers never succeed.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَلَقَدۡ هَمَّتۡ بِهِۦۖ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوۡلَآ أَن رَّءَا بُرۡهَٰنَ رَبِّهِۦۚ كَذَٰلِكَ لِنَصۡرِفَ عَنۡهُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَٱلۡفَحۡشَآءَۚ إِنَّهُۥ مِنۡ عِبَادِنَا ٱلۡمُخۡلَصِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-laqad hammat bihee Wa-hamma bihaa law-laaa ar ra-aa burhaana rabbih; kazaalika linasrifa 'anhu sooo'a walfa-hshaaa'; innahoo min 'ibaadi-nal mukhlaseen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And she certainly determined [to seduce] him, and he would have inclined to her had he not seen the proof of his Lord. And thus [it was] that We should avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: She advanced towards him, and he would have done likewise, had he not seen a sign from his Lord. This is how We kept evil and indecency away from him, for he was truly one of Our chosen servants.

ayahs.textArabic: وَٱسۡتَبَقَا ٱلۡبَابَ وَقَدَّتۡ قَمِيصَهُۥ مِن دُبُرٖ وَأَلۡفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَا ٱلۡبَابِۚ قَالَتۡ مَا جَزَآءُ مَنۡ أَرَادَ بِأَهۡلِكَ سُوٓءًا إِلَّآ أَن يُسۡجَنَ أَوۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wastabaqal baaba Wa-qaddat qameesahoo min duburinw Wa-alfayaa saiyidahaa ladal baab; qaalat maa jazaaa'u man araada bi ahlika sooo'an illaaa any-yusjana aw azaabun 'aleem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And they both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back, and they found her husband at the door. She said, "What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your wife but that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?"
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They raced for the door and she tore his shirt from the back, only to find her husband at the door. She cried, “What is the penalty for someone who tried to violate your wife, except imprisonment or a painful punishment?”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ هِيَ رَٰوَدَتۡنِي عَن نَّفۡسِيۚ وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٞ مِّنۡ أَهۡلِهَآ إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٖ فَصَدَقَتۡ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala hiya raawadatnee 'an nafsee Wa-shahida shaahidum min ahlihaa in kaana qameesuhoo qudda min qubulin fasadaqat Wa-huwa minal kaazibeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: [Joseph] said, "It was she who sought to seduce me." And a witness from her family testified. "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Joseph responded, “It was she who tried to seduce me.” And a witness from her own family testified: “If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is a liar.

ayahs.textArabic: وَإِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٖ فَكَذَبَتۡ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-in kaana qameesuhoo qudda min duburin fakazabat Wa-huwa minas saadiqeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: But if it is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is truthful.”

ayahs.textArabic: فَلَمَّا رَءَا قَمِيصَهُۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٖ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ مِن كَيۡدِكُنَّۖ إِنَّ كَيۡدَكُنَّ عَظِيمٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Falammaa ra-aa qamee-sahoo qudda min duburin qaala innahoo min kaidikunna inna kaidakunna 'azeem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: So when her husband saw his shirt torn from the back, he said, "Indeed, it is of the women's plan. Indeed, your plan is great.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: So when her husband saw that Joseph’s shirt was torn from the back, he said ˹to her˺, “This must be ˹an example˺ of the cunning of you ˹women˺! Indeed, your cunning is so shrewd!

ayahs.textArabic: يُوسُفُ أَعۡرِضۡ عَنۡ هَٰذَاۚ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرِي لِذَنۢبِكِۖ إِنَّكِ كُنتِ مِنَ ٱلۡخَاطِـِٔينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Yoosufu a'rid 'an haaza wastaghfiree li-zanbiki innaki kunti minal khaati'een
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Joseph, ignore this. And, [my wife], ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you were of the sinful."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: O Joseph! Forget about this. And you ˹O wife˺! Seek forgiveness for your sin. It certainly has been your fault.”

ayahs.textArabic: ۞ وَقَالَ نِسۡوَةٞ فِي ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ ٱمۡرَأَتُ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ تُرَٰوِدُ فَتَىٰهَا عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦۖ قَدۡ شَغَفَهَا حُبًّاۖ إِنَّا لَنَرَىٰهَا فِي ضَلَٰلٖ مُّبِينٖ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-qaala niswatun fil madeenatim ra-atul 'Azeezi turaawidu fataahaa 'an nafsihee qad shaghafahaa hubbaa; innaa lana-raahaa fee dalaalim mubeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And women in the city said, "The wife of al-'Azeez is seeking to seduce her slave boy; he has impassioned her with love. Indeed, we see her [to be] in clear error."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Some women of the city gossiped, “The Chief Minister’s wife is trying to seduce her slave-boy. Love for him has plagued her heart. Indeed, we see that she is clearly mistaken.”

ayahs.textArabic: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتۡ بِمَكۡرِهِنَّ أَرۡسَلَتۡ إِلَيۡهِنَّ وَأَعۡتَدَتۡ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَـٔٗا وَءَاتَتۡ كُلَّ وَٰحِدَةٖ مِّنۡهُنَّ سِكِّينٗا وَقَالَتِ ٱخۡرُجۡ عَلَيۡهِنَّۖ فَلَمَّا رَأَيۡنَهُۥٓ أَكۡبَرۡنَهُۥ وَقَطَّعۡنَ أَيۡدِيَهُنَّ وَقُلۡنَ حَٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا هَٰذَا بَشَرًا إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا مَلَكٞ كَرِيمٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Falammaa sami'at bimak-rihinna arsalat ilaihinna Wa-a'tadat lahunna muttaka-anw Wa-aatat kulla waahidatim min-hunna sikkeenanw Wa-qaala-tikh ruj 'alaihinna falammaa ra-aynahooo akbarnahoo Wa-qatta'na aydiyahunna Wa-qulna haasha lillaahi maa haaza basharaa; in haazaaa illaa malakun kareem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: So when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared for them a banquet and gave each one of them a knife and said [to Joseph], "Come out before them." And when they saw him, they greatly admired him and cut their hands and said, "Perfect is Allah! This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: When she heard about their gossip, she invited them and set a banquet for them. She gave each one a knife, then said ˹to Joseph˺, “Come out before them.” When they saw him, they were so stunned ˹by his beauty˺ that they cut their hands, and exclaimed, “Good God! This cannot be human; this must be a noble angel!”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَتۡ فَذَٰلِكُنَّ ٱلَّذِي لُمۡتُنَّنِي فِيهِۖ وَلَقَدۡ رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦ فَٱسۡتَعۡصَمَۖ وَلَئِن لَّمۡ يَفۡعَلۡ مَآ ءَامُرُهُۥ لَيُسۡجَنَنَّ وَلَيَكُونٗا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaalat fazaalikunnal lazee lumtunnanee feeh; Wa-laqad raawattuhoo 'an nafsihee fasta'sam; Wa-la'il lam yaf'al maaa aamuruhoo la-yusjananna Wa-la-yakoonam minas saaghireen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: She said, "That is the one about whom you blamed me. And I certainly sought to seduce him, but he firmly refused; and if he will not do what I order him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be of those debased."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: She said, “This is the one for whose love you criticized me! I did try to seduce him but he ˹firmly˺ refused. And if he does not do what I order him to, he will certainly be imprisoned and ˹fully˺ disgraced.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱلسِّجۡنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا يَدۡعُونَنِيٓ إِلَيۡهِۖ وَإِلَّا تَصۡرِفۡ عَنِّي كَيۡدَهُنَّ أَصۡبُ إِلَيۡهِنَّ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala rabbis sijnu ahabbu ilaiyya mimma yad'oo-naneee 'ilaihi Wa-illaa tasrif 'annee kaidahunna asbu ilaihinna Wa-akum minal jaahileen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: He said, "My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their plan, I might incline toward them and [thus] be of the ignorant."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Joseph prayed, “My Lord! I would rather be in jail than do what they invite me to. And if You do not turn their cunning away from me, I might yield to them and fall into ignorance.”

ayahs.textArabic: فَٱسۡتَجَابَ لَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ فَصَرَفَ عَنۡهُ كَيۡدَهُنَّۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Fastajaaba lahoo rabbuhoo fasarafa 'anhu kaidahunn; innahoo huwas Samee'ul 'Aleem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: So his Lord responded to him and averted from him their plan. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: So his Lord responded to him, turning their cunning away from him. Surely He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

ayahs.textArabic: ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا رَأَوُاْ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَيَسۡجُنُنَّهُۥ حَتَّىٰ حِينٖ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Summa badaa lahum min ba'di maa ra-awul Aayaati layasjununnahoo hatta heen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs that al-'Azeez should surely imprison him for a time.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And so it occurred to those in charge, despite seeing all the proofs ˹of his innocence˺, that he should be imprisoned for a while.

ayahs.textArabic: وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ ٱلسِّجۡنَ فَتَيَانِۖ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَآ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰنِيٓ أَعۡصِرُ خَمۡرٗاۖ وَقَالَ ٱلۡأٓخَرُ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰنِيٓ أَحۡمِلُ فَوۡقَ رَأۡسِي خُبۡزٗا تَأۡكُلُ ٱلطَّيۡرُ مِنۡهُۖ نَبِّئۡنَا بِتَأۡوِيلِهِۦٓۖ إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-dakhala ma'a hussijna fata-yaan; qaala ahaduhumaaa inneee araaneee a'siru khamranw Wa-qaalal aakharu inneee araaneee ahmilu fawqa ra'see khubzan ta'kulut tairu minhu; nabbi'naa bi-ta'weelih; innaa naraaka minal muhsineen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And there entered the prison with him two young men. One of them said, "Indeed, I have seen myself [in a dream] pressing wine." The other said, "Indeed, I have seen myself carrying upon my head [some] bread, from which the birds were eating. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you to be of those who do good."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And two other servants went to jail with Joseph. One of them said, “I dreamt I was pressing wine.” The other said, “I dreamt I was carrying ˹some˺ bread on my head, from which birds were eating.” ˹Then both said,˺ “Tell us their interpretation, for we surely see you as one of the good-doers.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ لَا يَأۡتِيكُمَا طَعَامٞ تُرۡزَقَانِهِۦٓ إِلَّا نَبَّأۡتُكُمَا بِتَأۡوِيلِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَن يَأۡتِيَكُمَاۚ ذَٰلِكُمَا مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِي رَبِّيٓۚ إِنِّي تَرَكۡتُ مِلَّةَ قَوۡمٖ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَهُم بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ كَٰفِرُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala laa ya'teekumaa ta'aamun turzaqaaniheee illaa nabba'tukumaa bi-ta'weelihee; qabla aien ya'ti-yakumaa; zaalikumaa mimmaa 'allamanee rabbee; innee taraktu millata qawmil laa yu'minoona billaahi wahum bil-aakhirati hum kaafiroon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: He said, "You will not receive food that is provided to you except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Joseph replied, “I can even tell you what kind of meal you will be served before you receive it. This ˹knowledge˺ is from what my Lord has taught me. I have shunned the faith of a people who disbelieve in Allah and deny the Hereafter.

ayahs.textArabic: وَٱتَّبَعۡتُ مِلَّةَ ءَابَآءِيٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَۚ مَا كَانَ لَنَآ أَن نُّشۡرِكَ بِٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءٖۚ ذَٰلِكَ مِن فَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡنَا وَعَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَشۡكُرُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wattaba'tu millata aabaaa'eee Ibraaheema Wa-Iss-haaqa Wa-Ya'qoob; maa kaana lanaaa an nushrika billaahi min shai'; zaalika min fadlil laahi 'alainaa Wa-'alan naasi Wa-laakinna aksaran naasi laa yashkuroon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. And it was not for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from the favor of Allah upon us and upon the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: I follow the faith of my fathers: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It is not ˹right˺ for us to associate anything with Allah ˹in worship˺. This is part of Allah’s grace upon us and humanity, but most people are not grateful.

ayahs.textArabic: يَٰصَٰحِبَيِ ٱلسِّجۡنِ ءَأَرۡبَابٞ مُّتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيۡرٌ أَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّارُ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Yaa-saahibayis sijni 'a-arbaabum mutafarriqoona khayrun amil laahul waahidul qahhaar
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: O [my] two companions of prison, are separate lords better or Allah, the One, the Prevailing?
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: O my fellow-prisoners! Which is far better: many different lords or Allah—the One, the Supreme?

ayahs.textArabic: مَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَسۡمَآءٗ سَمَّيۡتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلۡطَٰنٍۚ إِنِ ٱلۡحُكۡمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Maa ta'budoona min doonihee illaaa asmaaa'an sam maitumoohaaa antum Wa-aabaaa'ukum maaa anzalal laahu bihaa min sultan; inilhukmu illaa lillaah; amara allaa ta'budooo illaaa iyyaah; zaalikad deenul qaiyimu Wa-laakinna aksaran naasi laa ya'lamoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: You worship not besides Him except [mere] names you have named them, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority. Legislation is not but for Allah. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Whatever ˹idols˺ you worship instead of Him are mere names which you and your forefathers have made up—a practice Allah has never authorized. It is only Allah Who decides. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the upright faith, but most people do not know.

ayahs.textArabic: يَٰصَٰحِبَيِ ٱلسِّجۡنِ أَمَّآ أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسۡقِي رَبَّهُۥ خَمۡرٗاۖ وَأَمَّا ٱلۡأٓخَرُ فَيُصۡلَبُ فَتَأۡكُلُ ٱلطَّيۡرُ مِن رَّأۡسِهِۦۚ قُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ ٱلَّذِي فِيهِ تَسۡتَفۡتِيَانِ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Yaa-saahibayis sijni ammaaa ahadukumaa fa-yasqee rabbahoo khamranw Wa-ammal aakharu fa-yuslabu fata'kulut tairu mir ra'sih; qudiyal amrul lazee feehi tastaftiyaan
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: O two companions of prison, as for one of you, he will give drink to his master of wine; but as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: “O my fellow-prisoners! ˹The first˺ one of you will serve wine to his master, and the other will be crucified and the birds will eat from his head. The matter about which you inquired has been decided.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَقَالَ لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ أَنَّهُۥ نَاجٖ مِّنۡهُمَا ٱذۡكُرۡنِي عِندَ رَبِّكَ فَأَنسَىٰهُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ ذِكۡرَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِي ٱلسِّجۡنِ بِضۡعَ سِنِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-qaala lillazee zanna annahoo najim minhumaz kurnee 'inda rabbika fa-ansaahush Shaitaanu zikra Rabbihee falabisa fis sijni bid'a sineen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And he said to the one whom he knew would go free, "Mention me before your master." But Satan made him forget the mention [to] his master, and Joseph remained in prison several years.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Then he said to the one he knew would survive, “Mention me in the presence of your master.” But Satan made him forget to mention Joseph to his master, so he remained in prison for several years.

ayahs.textArabic: وَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰ سَبۡعَ بَقَرَٰتٖ سِمَانٖ يَأۡكُلُهُنَّ سَبۡعٌ عِجَافٞ وَسَبۡعَ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضۡرٖ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٖۖ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡمَلَأُ أَفۡتُونِي فِي رُءۡيَٰيَ إِن كُنتُمۡ لِلرُّءۡيَا تَعۡبُرُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-qaalal maliku inneee araa sab'a baqaraatin simaanien ya'kuluhunna sab'un 'ijaafunw Wa-sab'a sumbulaatin khudrinw Wa-ukhara yaabisaat; yaaa-ayyuhal mala-u aftoonee fee ru'yaaya in kuntum lirru'yaa ta'buroon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And [subsequently] the king said, "Indeed, I have seen [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry. O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you should interpret visions."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And ˹one day˺ the King said, “I dreamt of seven fat cows eaten up by seven skinny ones; and seven green ears of grain and ˹seven˺ others dry. O chiefs! Tell me the meaning of my dream if you can interpret dreams.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُوٓاْ أَضۡغَٰثُ أَحۡلَٰمٖۖ وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِتَأۡوِيلِ ٱلۡأَحۡلَٰمِ بِعَٰلِمِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaalooo adghaasu ahlaa-minw Wa-maa nahnu bi-ta'weelil ahlaami bi'aalimeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "[It is but] a mixture of false dreams, and we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They replied, “These are confused visions and we do not know the interpretation of such dreams.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِي نَجَا مِنۡهُمَا وَٱدَّكَرَ بَعۡدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا۠ أُنَبِّئُكُم بِتَأۡوِيلِهِۦ فَأَرۡسِلُونِ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-qaalal lazee najaa minhumaa waddakara ba'da ummatin ana unabbi'ukum bi-ta'weelihee fa-arsiloon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: But the one who was freed and remembered after a time said, "I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: ˹Finally,˺ the surviving ex-prisoner remembered ˹Joseph˺ after a long time and said, “I will tell you its interpretation, so send me forth ˹to Joseph˺.”

ayahs.textArabic: يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا ٱلصِّدِّيقُ أَفۡتِنَا فِي سَبۡعِ بَقَرَٰتٖ سِمَانٖ يَأۡكُلُهُنَّ سَبۡعٌ عِجَافٞ وَسَبۡعِ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضۡرٖ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٖ لَّعَلِّيٓ أَرۡجِعُ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Yoosufu ayyuhas siddeequ aftinaa fee sab'i baqaraatin simaaniny ya'kuluhunna sab'un 'ijaafunw Wa-sabi'i sumbulaatin khudrinw Wa-ukhara yaabisaatil la'alleee arji'u ilan naasi la'allahum ya'lamoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: [He said], "Joseph, O man of truth, explain to us about seven fat cows eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry - that I may return to the people; perhaps they will know [about you]."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: ˹He said,˺ “Joseph, O man of truth! Interpret for us ˹the dream of˺ seven fat cows eaten up by seven skinny ones; and seven green ears of grain and ˹seven˺ others dry, so that I may return to the people and let them know.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ تَزۡرَعُونَ سَبۡعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبٗا فَمَا حَصَدتُّمۡ فَذَرُوهُ فِي سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلٗا مِّمَّا تَأۡكُلُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala tazra'oona sab'a sineena da-aban famaa hasattum fazaroohu fee sumbu-liheee illaa qaleelam mimmaa ta'kuloon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: [Joseph] said, "You will plant for seven years consecutively; and what you harvest leave in its spikes, except a little from which you will eat.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Joseph replied, “You will plant ˹grain˺ for seven consecutive years, leaving in the ear whatever you will harvest, except for the little you will eat.

ayahs.textArabic: ثُمَّ يَأۡتِي مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ سَبۡعٞ شِدَادٞ يَأۡكُلۡنَ مَا قَدَّمۡتُمۡ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلٗا مِّمَّا تُحۡصِنُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Thumma ya'tee mim ba'di zaalika sab'un shidaaduny ya'kulna maa qaddamtum lahunna illaa qaleelam mimma tuhsinoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Then will come after that seven difficult [years] which will consume what you saved for them, except a little from which you will store.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Then after that will come seven years of great hardship which will consume whatever you have saved, except the little you will store ˹for seed˺.

ayahs.textArabic: ثُمَّ يَأۡتِي مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ عَامٞ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعۡصِرُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Thumma ya'tee mim ba'di zalika 'aamun feehi yughaa-sun naasu Wa-feehi ya'siroon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Then will come after that a year in which the people will be given rain and in which they will press [olives and grapes]."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Then after that will come a year in which people will receive abundant rain and they will press ˹oil and wine˺.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱئۡتُونِي بِهِۦۖ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُ ٱلرَّسُولُ قَالَ ٱرۡجِعۡ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَسۡـَٔلۡهُ مَا بَالُ ٱلنِّسۡوَةِ ٱلَّٰتِي قَطَّعۡنَ أَيۡدِيَهُنَّۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي بِكَيۡدِهِنَّ عَلِيمٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-qaalal maliku 'toonee bihee falammaa jaaa'ahur rasoolu qaalar ji ilaa rabbika fas'alhu maa baalun niswatil laatee qatta'na aydiyahunn; inna Rabbee bikaidihinna 'Aleem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And the king said, "Bring him to me." But when the messenger came to him, [Joseph] said, "Return to your master and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plan."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: The King ˹then˺ said, “Bring him to me.” When the messenger came to him, Joseph said, “Go back to your master and ask him about the case of the women who cut their hands. Surely my Lord has ˹full˺ knowledge of their cunning.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ مَا خَطۡبُكُنَّ إِذۡ رَٰوَدتُّنَّ يُوسُفَ عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦۚ قُلۡنَ حَٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا عَلِمۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ مِن سُوٓءٖۚ قَالَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتُ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡـَٰٔنَ حَصۡحَصَ ٱلۡحَقُّ أَنَا۠ رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala maa khatbukunna iz raawattunna Yoosufa 'an nafsih; qulna haasha lillaahi maa 'alimnaa 'alaihi min sooo'; qaalatim ra-atul 'Azeezil 'aana hashasal haqq, ana raawat-tuhoo 'an nafsihee Wa-innahoo laminas saadiqeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Said [the king to the women], "What was your condition when you sought to seduce Joseph?" They said, "Perfect is Allah! We know about him no evil." The wife of al-'Azeez said, "Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: The King asked ˹the women˺, “What did you get when you tried to seduce Joseph?” They replied, “Allah forbid! We know nothing indecent about him.” Then the Chief Minister’s wife admitted, “Now the truth has come to light. It was I who tried to seduce him, and he is surely truthful.

ayahs.textArabic: ذَٰلِكَ لِيَعۡلَمَ أَنِّي لَمۡ أَخُنۡهُ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي كَيۡدَ ٱلۡخَآئِنِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Zaalika liya'lama annee lam akhunhu bilghaibi Wa-annal laaha laa yahdee kaidal khaaa'ineen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: That is so al-'Azeez will know that I did not betray him in [his] absence and that Allah does not guide the plan of betrayers.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: From this, Joseph should know that I did not speak dishonestly about him in his absence, for Allah certainly does not guide the scheming of the dishonest.

ayahs.textArabic: ۞ وَمَآ أُبَرِّئُ نَفۡسِيٓۚ إِنَّ ٱلنَّفۡسَ لَأَمَّارَةُۢ بِٱلسُّوٓءِ إِلَّا مَا رَحِمَ رَبِّيٓۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-maa ubarri'u nafsee; innan nafsa la-ammaaratum bissooo'i illaa maa rahima Rabbee; inna Rabbee Ghafoorur Raheem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And I do not seek to free myself from blame, for indeed the soul is ever inclined to evil, except those shown mercy by my Lord. Surely my Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱئۡتُونِي بِهِۦٓ أَسۡتَخۡلِصۡهُ لِنَفۡسِيۖ فَلَمَّا كَلَّمَهُۥ قَالَ إِنَّكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ لَدَيۡنَا مَكِينٌ أَمِينٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-qaalal maliku' toonee biheee astakhlishu linafsee falammaa kallamahoo qaala innakal yawma ladainaa makeenun ameen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And the king said, "Bring him to me; I will appoint him exclusively for myself." And when he spoke to him, he said, "Indeed, you are today established [in position] and trusted."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: The King said, “Bring him to me. I will employ him exclusively in my service.” And when Joseph spoke to him, the King said, “Today you are highly esteemed and fully trusted by us.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ ٱجۡعَلۡنِي عَلَىٰ خَزَآئِنِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ إِنِّي حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaalaj 'alnee 'alaa khazaaa'inil ardi innee hafeezun 'aleem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: [Joseph] said, "Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I will be a knowing guardian."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Joseph proposed, “Put me in charge of the store-houses of the land, for I am truly reliable and adept.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَتَبَوَّأُ مِنۡهَا حَيۡثُ يَشَآءُۚ نُصِيبُ بِرَحۡمَتِنَا مَن نَّشَآءُۖ وَلَا نُضِيعُ أَجۡرَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-kazaalika makkannaa li-Yoosufa fil ardi yatabawwa'u minhaa haisu yashaaaa'; nuseebu birahmatinaa man nashaaa'u Wa-laa nudee'u ajral muhsineen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And thus We established Joseph in the land to settle therein wherever he willed. We touch with Our mercy whom We will, and We do not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: This is how We established Joseph in the land to settle wherever he pleased. We shower Our mercy on whoever We will, and We never discount the reward of the good-doers.

ayahs.textArabic: وَلَأَجۡرُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ خَيۡرٞ لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَكَانُواْ يَتَّقُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-la-ajrul Aakhirati khairul lillazeena aamanoo Wa-kaanoo yattaqoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believed and were fearing Allah.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And the reward of the Hereafter is far better for those who are faithful and are mindful ˹of Allah˺.

ayahs.textArabic: وَجَآءَ إِخۡوَةُ يُوسُفَ فَدَخَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِ فَعَرَفَهُمۡ وَهُمۡ لَهُۥ مُنكِرُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-jaaa'a ikhwatu Yoosufa fadakhaloo 'alaihi fa'arafahum Wa-hum lahoo munkiroon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And the brothers of Joseph came [seeking food], and they entered upon him; and he recognized them, but he was to them unknown.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And Joseph’s brothers came and entered his presence. He recognized them but they were unaware of who he really was.

ayahs.textArabic: وَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمۡ قَالَ ٱئۡتُونِي بِأَخٖ لَّكُم مِّنۡ أَبِيكُمۡۚ أَلَا تَرَوۡنَ أَنِّيٓ أُوفِي ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَأَنَا۠ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡمُنزِلِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-lammaa jahhazahum bijahaazihim qaala' toonee bi-akhil lakum min abeekum; alaa tarawna anneee oofil kaila Wa-ana khairul munzileen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And when he had furnished them with their supplies, he said, "Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do not you see that I give full measure and that I am the best of accommodators?
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: When he had provided them with their supplies, he demanded, “Bring me your brother on your father’s side. Do you not see that I give full measure and I am the best of hosts?

ayahs.textArabic: فَإِن لَّمۡ تَأۡتُونِي بِهِۦ فَلَا كَيۡلَ لَكُمۡ عِندِي وَلَا تَقۡرَبُونِ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Fa-il lam taatoonee bihee falaa kaila lakum 'indee Wa-laa taqraboon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: But if you do not bring him to me, no measure will there be [hereafter] for you from me, nor will you approach me."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: But if you do not bring him to me ˹next time˺, I will have no grain for you, nor will you ever come close to me again.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ سَنُرَٰوِدُ عَنۡهُ أَبَاهُ وَإِنَّا لَفَٰعِلُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo sanuraawidu 'anhu abaahu Wa-innaa lafaa'iloon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "We will attempt to dissuade his father from [keeping] him, and indeed, we will do [it]."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They promised, “We will try to convince his father to let him come. We will certainly do ˹our best˺.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَقَالَ لِفِتۡيَٰنِهِ ٱجۡعَلُواْ بِضَٰعَتَهُمۡ فِي رِحَالِهِمۡ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَعۡرِفُونَهَآ إِذَا ٱنقَلَبُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِمۡ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-qaala lifityaanihij 'aloo bidaa'atahum fee rihaalihim la'allahum ya'rifoonahaaa izan qalabooo ilaaa ahlihim la'allahum yarji'oon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And [Joseph] said to his servants, "Put their merchandise into their saddlebags so they might recognize it when they have gone back to their people that perhaps they will [again] return."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Joseph ordered his servants to put his brothers’ money back into their saddlebags so that they would find it when they returned to their family and perhaps they would come back.

ayahs.textArabic: فَلَمَّا رَجَعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِيهِمۡ قَالُواْ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مُنِعَ مِنَّا ٱلۡكَيۡلُ فَأَرۡسِلۡ مَعَنَآ أَخَانَا نَكۡتَلۡ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Falammaa raja'ooo ilaaa abeehim qaaloo yaaa-abaanaa muni'a minnal kailu fa-arsil ma'anaaa akhaanaa naktal Wa-innaa lahoo lahaafizoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: So when they returned to their father, they said, "O our father, [further] measure has been denied to us, so send with us our brother [that] we will be given measure. And indeed, we will be his guardians."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: When Joseph’s brothers returned to their father, they pleaded, “O our father! We have been denied ˹further˺ supplies. So send our brother with us so that we may receive our measure, and we will definitely watch over him.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ هَلۡ ءَامَنُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ إِلَّا كَمَآ أَمِنتُكُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَخِيهِ مِن قَبۡلُ فَٱللَّهُ خَيۡرٌ حَٰفِظٗاۖ وَهُوَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala hal aamanukum 'alaihi illaa kamaa amintukum 'alaaa akheehi min qabl; fal-laahu khairun haafizanw Wa-Huwa arhamur Raahimeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: He said, "Should I entrust you with him except [under coercion] as I entrusted you with his brother before? But Allah is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: He responded, “Should I trust you with him as I once trusted you with his brother ˹Joseph˺? But ˹only˺ Allah is the best Protector, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَلَمَّا فَتَحُواْ مَتَٰعَهُمۡ وَجَدُواْ بِضَٰعَتَهُمۡ رُدَّتۡ إِلَيۡهِمۡۖ قَالُواْ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مَا نَبۡغِيۖ هَٰذِهِۦ بِضَٰعَتُنَا رُدَّتۡ إِلَيۡنَاۖ وَنَمِيرُ أَهۡلَنَا وَنَحۡفَظُ أَخَانَا وَنَزۡدَادُ كَيۡلَ بَعِيرٖۖ ذَٰلِكَ كَيۡلٞ يَسِيرٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-lammaa fatahoo mataa-'ahum wajadoo bidaa'atahum ruddat ilaihim qaaloo yaaa-abaanaa maa nabghee; haazihee bida-'atunaa ruddat ilainaa Wa-nameeru ahlanaa Wa-nahfazu akhaanaa Wa-nazdaadu kaila ba'eer; zaalika kailuien yaseer
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what [more] could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. And we will obtain supplies for our family and protect our brother and obtain an increase of a camel's load; that is an easy measurement."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: When they opened their bags, they discovered that their money had been returned to them. They argued, “O our father! What more can we ask for? Here is our money, fully returned to us. Now we can buy more food for our family. We will watch over our brother, and obtain an extra camel-load of grain. That load can be easily secured.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ لَنۡ أُرۡسِلَهُۥ مَعَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ تُؤۡتُونِ مَوۡثِقٗا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لَتَأۡتُنَّنِي بِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن يُحَاطَ بِكُمۡۖ فَلَمَّآ ءَاتَوۡهُ مَوۡثِقَهُمۡ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala lan ursilahoo ma'akum hattaa tu'tooni mawsiqam minal laahis lataa-tunnanee biheee illaaa aien yuhaata bikum falammaaa aatawhu mawsiqahum qaalal laahu 'alaa maa naqoolu Wakeel
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: [Jacob] said, "Never will I send him with you until you give me a promise by Allah that you will bring him [back] to me, unless you should be surrounded by enemies." And when they had given their promise, he said, "Allah, over what we say, is Witness."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Jacob insisted, “I will not send him with you until you give me a solemn oath by Allah that you will certainly bring him back to me, unless you are totally overpowered.” Then after they had given him their oaths, he concluded, “Allah is a Witness to what we have said.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَقَالَ يَٰبَنِيَّ لَا تَدۡخُلُواْ مِنۢ بَابٖ وَٰحِدٖ وَٱدۡخُلُواْ مِنۡ أَبۡوَٰبٖ مُّتَفَرِّقَةٖۖ وَمَآ أُغۡنِي عَنكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءٍۖ إِنِ ٱلۡحُكۡمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِۖ عَلَيۡهِ تَوَكَّلۡتُۖ وَعَلَيۡهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُتَوَكِّلُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-qaala yaa-baniyya laa tadkhuloo mim baabinw waa-hidinw wadkhuloo min abwaabim mutafarriqah; Wa-maaa ughnee 'ankum minal laahi min shai'in; inil hukmu illaa lillaahi 'alaihi tawakkaltu Wa-'alaihi fal-yatawakkalil Mutawakkiloon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And he said, "O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from different gates; and I cannot avail you against [the decree of] Allah at all. The decision is only for Allah; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let those who would rely [indeed] rely."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: He then instructed ˹them˺, “O my sons! Do not enter ˹the city˺ all through one gate, but through separate gates. I cannot help you against ˹what is destined by˺ Allah in the least. It is only Allah Who decides. In Him I put my trust. And in Him let the faithful put their trust.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُواْ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ أَمَرَهُمۡ أَبُوهُم مَّا كَانَ يُغۡنِي عَنۡهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِلَّا حَاجَةٗ فِي نَفۡسِ يَعۡقُوبَ قَضَىٰهَاۚ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَذُو عِلۡمٖ لِّمَا عَلَّمۡنَٰهُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-lammaa dakhaloo min haisu amarahum aboohum maa kaana yughnee 'anhum minal laahi min shai'in illaa haajatan fee nafsi Ya'qooba qadaahaa; Wa-innahoo lazoo 'ilmil limaa 'allamnaahu Wa-laakinna aksaran naasi laa ya'lamoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And when they entered from where their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against Allah at all except [it was] a need within the soul of Jacob, which he satisfied. And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Then when they entered as their father had instructed them, this did not help them against ˹the Will of˺ Allah whatsoever. It was just a desire in Jacob’s heart which he satisfied. He was truly blessed with ˹great˺ knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most people have no knowledge.

ayahs.textArabic: وَلَمَّا دَخَلُواْ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ ءَاوَىٰٓ إِلَيۡهِ أَخَاهُۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَنَا۠ أَخُوكَ فَلَا تَبۡتَئِسۡ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-lammaa dakhaloo 'alaa Yoosufa aawaaa ilaihi akhaahu qaala inneee ana akhooka falaa tabta'is bimaa kaanoo ya'maloon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother to himself; he said, "Indeed, I am your brother, so do not despair over what they used to do [to me]."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: When they entered Joseph’s presence, he called his brother ˹Benjamin˺ aside, and confided ˹to him˺, “I am indeed your brother ˹Joseph˺! So do not feel distressed about what they have been doing.”

ayahs.textArabic: فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُم بِجَهَازِهِمۡ جَعَلَ ٱلسِّقَايَةَ فِي رَحۡلِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَيَّتُهَا ٱلۡعِيرُ إِنَّكُمۡ لَسَٰرِقُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Falammaa jahhazahum bijahaazihim ja'alas siqaayata fee rahli akheehi summa azzana mu'azzinun ayyatuhal 'eeru innakum lasaariqoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: So when he had furnished them with their supplies, he put the [gold measuring] bowl into the bag of his brother. Then an announcer called out, "O caravan, indeed you are thieves."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: When Joseph had provided them with supplies, he slipped the royal cup into his brother’s bag. Then a herald cried, “O people of the caravan! You must be thieves!”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ وَأَقۡبَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِم مَّاذَا تَفۡقِدُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo Wa-aqbaloo 'alaihim maazaa tafqidoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said while approaching them, "What is it you are missing?"
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They asked, turning back, “What have you lost?”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ نَفۡقِدُ صُوَاعَ ٱلۡمَلِكِ وَلِمَن جَآءَ بِهِۦ حِمۡلُ بَعِيرٖ وَأَنَا۠ بِهِۦ زَعِيمٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo nafqidu suwaa'al maliki Wa-liman jaaa'a bihee himlu ba'eerinw Wa-ana bihee za'eem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "We are missing the measure of the king. And for he who produces it is [the reward of] a camel's load, and I am responsible for it."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: The herald ˹along with the guards˺ replied, “We have lost the King’s measuring cup. And whoever brings it will be awarded a camel-load ˹of grain˺. I guarantee it.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتُم مَّا جِئۡنَا لِنُفۡسِدَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا كُنَّا سَٰرِقِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo tallaahi laqad 'alimtum maa ji'na linufsida fil ardi Wa-maa kunnaa saariqeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "By Allah, you have certainly known that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and we have not been thieves."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Joseph’s brothers replied, “By Allah! You know well that we did not come to cause trouble in the land, nor are we thieves.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ فَمَا جَزَٰٓؤُهُۥٓ إِن كُنتُمۡ كَٰذِبِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo famaa jazaaa'u-hooo in kuntum kaazibeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: The accusers said, "Then what would be its recompense if you should be liars?"
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Joseph’s men asked, “What should be the price for theft, if you are lying?”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ جَزَٰٓؤُهُۥ مَن وُجِدَ فِي رَحۡلِهِۦ فَهُوَ جَزَٰٓؤُهُۥۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo jazaaa'uhoo manw wujida fee rahlihee fahuwa jazaaa'uh; kazaalika najziz zaalimeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: [The brothers] said, "Its recompense is that he in whose bag it is found - he [himself] will be its recompense. Thus do we recompense the wrongdoers."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Joseph’s brothers responded, “The price will be ˹the enslavement of˺ the one in whose bag the cup is found. That is how we punish the wrongdoers.”

ayahs.textArabic: فَبَدَأَ بِأَوۡعِيَتِهِمۡ قَبۡلَ وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَخۡرَجَهَا مِن وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِۚ كَذَٰلِكَ كِدۡنَا لِيُوسُفَۖ مَا كَانَ لِيَأۡخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِي دِينِ ٱلۡمَلِكِ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ نَرۡفَعُ دَرَجَٰتٖ مَّن نَّشَآءُۗ وَفَوۡقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلۡمٍ عَلِيمٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Fabada-a bi-aw'iyatihim qabla wi'aaa'i akheehi summas takhrajahaa minw wi-'aaa'i akheeh; kazaalika kidnaa li-Yoosuf; maa kaana liyaakhuza akhaahu fee deenil maliki illaaa aien yashaaa'al laah; narfa'u darajaatim man nashaaa'; Wa-fawqa kulli zee 'ilmin 'Aleem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: So he began [the search] with their bags before the bag of his brother; then he extracted it from the bag of his brother. Thus did We plan for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother within the religion of the king except that Allah willed. We raise in degrees whom We will, but over every possessor of knowledge is one [more] knowing.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Joseph began searching their bags before that of his brother ˹Benjamin˺, then brought it out of Benjamin’s bag. This is how We inspired Joseph to plan. He could not have taken his brother under the King’s law, but Allah had so willed. We elevate in rank whoever We will. But above those ranking in knowledge is the One All-Knowing.

ayahs.textArabic: ۞ قَالُوٓاْ إِن يَسۡرِقۡ فَقَدۡ سَرَقَ أَخٞ لَّهُۥ مِن قَبۡلُۚ فَأَسَرَّهَا يُوسُفُ فِي نَفۡسِهِۦ وَلَمۡ يُبۡدِهَا لَهُمۡۚ قَالَ أَنتُمۡ شَرّٞ مَّكَانٗاۖ وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا تَصِفُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo ien yasriq faqad saraqa akhul lahoo min qabl; fa-asarrahaa Yoosufu fee nafsihee Wa-lam yubdihaa lahum; qaala antum sharrum makaananw wallaahu a'lamu bimaa tasifoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "If he steals - a brother of his has stolen before." But Joseph kept it within himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, "You are worse in position, and Allah is most knowing of what you describe."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: ˹To distance themselves,˺ Joseph’s brothers argued, “If he has stolen, so did his ˹full˺ brother before.” But Joseph suppressed his outrage—revealing nothing to them—and said ˹to himself˺, “You are in such an evil position, and Allah knows best ˹the truth of˺ what you claim.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡعَزِيزُ إِنَّ لَهُۥٓ أَبٗا شَيۡخٗا كَبِيرٗا فَخُذۡ أَحَدَنَا مَكَانَهُۥٓۖ إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo yaaa-ayyuhal 'Azeezu inna lahooo aban shaikhan kabeeran fakhuz ahadanaa makaanahoo innaa naraaka minal muhsineen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "O 'Azeez, indeed he has a father [who is] an old man, so take one of us in place of him. Indeed, we see you as a doer of good."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They appealed, “O Chief Minister! He has a very old father, so take one of us instead. We surely see you as one of the good-doers.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ أَن نَّأۡخُذَ إِلَّا مَن وَجَدۡنَا مَتَٰعَنَا عِندَهُۥٓ إِنَّآ إِذٗا لَّظَٰلِمُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala ma'aazal laahi an naakhuza illaa manw wajadnaa mataa'anaa 'indahoo innaaa izal lazaalimoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: He said, "[I seek] the refuge of Allah [to prevent] that we take except him with whom we found our possession. Indeed, we would then be unjust."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Joseph responded, “Allah forbid that we should take other than the one with whom we found our property. Otherwise, we would surely be unjust.”

ayahs.textArabic: فَلَمَّا ٱسۡتَيۡـَٔسُواْ مِنۡهُ خَلَصُواْ نَجِيّٗاۖ قَالَ كَبِيرُهُمۡ أَلَمۡ تَعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ أَبَاكُمۡ قَدۡ أَخَذَ عَلَيۡكُم مَّوۡثِقٗا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمِن قَبۡلُ مَا فَرَّطتُمۡ فِي يُوسُفَۖ فَلَنۡ أَبۡرَحَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ حَتَّىٰ يَأۡذَنَ لِيٓ أَبِيٓ أَوۡ يَحۡكُمَ ٱللَّهُ لِيۖ وَهُوَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡحَٰكِمِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Falammas tay'asoo minhu khalasoo najiyyan qaala kabeeruhum alam ta'lamoon anna abaakum qad akhaza 'alaikum mawsiqam minal laahi Wa-min qablu maa farrattum fee Yoosufa falan abrahal arda hattaa yaazana leee abeee aw yahkumal laahu lee Wa-huwa khairul haakimeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: So when they had despaired of him, they secluded themselves in private consultation. The eldest of them said, "Do you not know that your father has taken upon you an oath by Allah and [that] before you failed in [your duty to] Joseph? So I will never leave [this] land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me, and He is the best of judges.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: When they lost all hope in him, they spoke privately. The eldest of them said, “Do you not know that your father had taken a solemn oath by Allah from you, nor how you failed him regarding Joseph before? So I am not leaving this land until my father allows me to, or Allah decides for me. For He is the Best of Judges.

ayahs.textArabic: ٱرۡجِعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِيكُمۡ فَقُولُواْ يَٰٓأَبَانَآ إِنَّ ٱبۡنَكَ سَرَقَ وَمَا شَهِدۡنَآ إِلَّا بِمَا عَلِمۡنَا وَمَا كُنَّا لِلۡغَيۡبِ حَٰفِظِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Irji'ooo ilaaa abeekum faqooloo yaaa-abaanaaa innab naka saraq; Wa-maa shahidnaaa illaa bimaa 'alimnaa Wa-maa kunnaa lilghaibi haafizeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Return to your father and say, "O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we did not testify except to what we knew. And we were not witnesses of the unseen,
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Return to your father and say, ‘O our father! Your son committed theft. We testify only to what we know. We could not guard against the unforeseen.

ayahs.textArabic: وَسۡـَٔلِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنَّا فِيهَا وَٱلۡعِيرَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَقۡبَلۡنَا فِيهَاۖ وَإِنَّا لَصَٰدِقُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Was'alil qaryatal latee kunnaa feehaa wal'eeral lateee aqbalnaa feehaa Wa-innaa lasaadiqoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And ask the city in which we were and the caravan in which we came - and indeed, we are truthful,"
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Ask ˹the people of˺ the land where we were and the caravan we travelled with. We are certainly telling the truth.’”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ بَلۡ سَوَّلَتۡ لَكُمۡ أَنفُسُكُمۡ أَمۡرٗاۖ فَصَبۡرٞ جَمِيلٌۖ عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَأۡتِيَنِي بِهِمۡ جَمِيعًاۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala bal sawwalat lakum anfusukum amran fasabrun jameelun 'asal laahu aien yaa-tiyanee bihim jamee'aa; innahoo Huwal 'Aleemul Hakeem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: [Jacob] said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. Perhaps Allah will bring them to me all together. Indeed it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: He cried, “No! Your souls must have tempted you to do something ˹evil˺. So ˹I am left with nothing but˺ beautiful patience! I trust Allah will return them all to me. Surely He ˹alone˺ is the All-Knowing, All-Wise.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَتَوَلَّىٰ عَنۡهُمۡ وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَسَفَىٰ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَٱبۡيَضَّتۡ عَيۡنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلۡحُزۡنِ فَهُوَ كَظِيمٞ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-tawallaa 'anhum Wa-qaala yaaa-asafaa 'alaa Yoosufa wabyaddat 'aynaahu minal huzni fahuwa kazeem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And he turned away from them and said, "Oh, my sorrow over Joseph," and his eyes became white from grief, for he was [of that] a suppressor.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: He turned away from them, lamenting, “Alas, poor Joseph!” And his eyes turned white out of the grief he suppressed.

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ تَفۡتَؤُاْ تَذۡكُرُ يُوسُفَ حَتَّىٰ تَكُونَ حَرَضًا أَوۡ تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَٰلِكِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo tallaahi tafta'u tazkuru Yoosufa hattaa takoona haradan aw takoona minal haalikeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "By Allah, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become fatally ill or become of those who perish."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They said, “By Allah! You will not cease to remember Joseph until you lose your health or ˹even˺ your life.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَشۡكُواْ بَثِّي وَحُزۡنِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala innamaaa ashkoo bassee Wa-huzneee ilal laahi Wa-a'lamu minal laahi maa laa ta'lamoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: He said, "I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: He replied, “I complain of my anguish and sorrow only to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know.

ayahs.textArabic: يَٰبَنِيَّ ٱذۡهَبُواْ فَتَحَسَّسُواْ مِن يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ وَلَا تَاْيۡـَٔسُواْ مِن رَّوۡحِ ٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يَاْيۡـَٔسُ مِن رَّوۡحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Yaa-baniyyaz haboo fatahassasoo mien Yoosufa Wa-akheehi Wa-laa tai'asoo mir rawhil laahi innahoo laa yai'asu mir rawhil laahi illal qawmul kaafiroon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: O my sons! Go and search ˹diligently˺ for Joseph and his brother. And do not lose hope in the mercy of Allah, for no one loses hope in Allah’s mercy except those with no faith.”

ayahs.textArabic: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِ قَالُواْ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡعَزِيزُ مَسَّنَا وَأَهۡلَنَا ٱلضُّرُّ وَجِئۡنَا بِبِضَٰعَةٖ مُّزۡجَىٰةٖ فَأَوۡفِ لَنَا ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَتَصَدَّقۡ عَلَيۡنَآۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُتَصَدِّقِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Falammaa dakhaloo 'alaihi qaaloo yaaa-ayyuhal 'Azeezu massanaa Wa-ahlanad durru Wa-ji'naa bibidaa 'timmuzjaatin fa-awfi lanal kaila Wa-tasaddaq 'alainaa innal laaha yajzil mutasaddiqeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: So when they entered upon Joseph, they said, "O 'Azeez, adversity has touched us and our family, and we have come with goods poor in quality, but give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: When they entered Joseph’s presence, they pleaded, “O Chief Minister! We and our family have been touched with hardship, and we have brought only a few worthless coins, but ˹please˺ give us our supplies in full and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ هَلۡ عَلِمۡتُم مَّا فَعَلۡتُم بِيُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ إِذۡ أَنتُمۡ جَٰهِلُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala hal 'alimtum maa fa'altum bi-Yoosufa Wa-akheehi iz antum jaahiloon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: He said, "Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?"
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: He asked, “Do you remember what you did to Joseph and his brother in your ignorance?”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُوٓاْ أَءِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ يُوسُفُۖ قَالَ أَنَا۠ يُوسُفُ وَهَٰذَآ أَخِيۖ قَدۡ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَآۖ إِنَّهُۥ مَن يَتَّقِ وَيَصۡبِرۡ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجۡرَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo 'a-innaka la-anta Yoosufu qaala ana Yoosufu Wa-haazaaa akhee qad mannal laahu 'alainaa innahoo mai yattaqi Wa-yasbir fa-innal laaha laa yudee'u ajral muhsineen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "Are you indeed Joseph?" He said "I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly favored us. Indeed, he who fears Allah and is patient, then indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They replied ˹in shock˺, “Are you really Joseph?” He said, “I am Joseph, and here is my brother ˹Benjamin˺! Allah has truly been gracious to us. Surely whoever is mindful ˹of Allah˺ and patient, then certainly Allah never discounts the reward of the good-doers.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدۡ ءَاثَرَكَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا وَإِن كُنَّا لَخَٰطِـِٔينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo tallaahi laqad aasarakal laahu 'alainaa Wa-in kunnaa lakhaati'een
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "By Allah, certainly has Allah preferred you over us, and indeed, we have been sinners."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They admitted, “By Allah! Allah has truly preferred you over us, and we have surely been sinful.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ لَا تَثۡرِيبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ يَغۡفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۖ وَهُوَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala laa tasreeba 'alaikumul yawma yaghfirul laahu lakum Wa-Huwa arhamur raahimeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: He said, "No blame will there be upon you today. Allah will forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Joseph said, “There is no blame on you today. May Allah forgive you! He is the Most Merciful of the merciful!

ayahs.textArabic: ٱذۡهَبُواْ بِقَمِيصِي هَٰذَا فَأَلۡقُوهُ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِ أَبِي يَأۡتِ بَصِيرٗا وَأۡتُونِي بِأَهۡلِكُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Izhaboo biqameesee haazaa fa-alqoohu 'alaa wajhi abee yaati baseeranw waatoonee bi-ahlikum ajma'een
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Take this, my shirt, and cast it over the face of my father; he will become seeing. And bring me your family, all together."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Go with this shirt of mine and cast it over my father’s face, and he will regain his sight. Then come back to me with your whole family.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَلَمَّا فَصَلَتِ ٱلۡعِيرُ قَالَ أَبُوهُمۡ إِنِّي لَأَجِدُ رِيحَ يُوسُفَۖ لَوۡلَآ أَن تُفَنِّدُونِ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-lammaa fasalatil 'eeru qaala aboohum innee la-ajidu reeha Yoosufa law-laaa an tufannidoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And when the caravan departed [from Egypt], their father said, "Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph [and would say that he was alive] if you did not think me weakened in mind."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: When the caravan departed ˹from Egypt˺, their father said ˹to those around him˺, “You may think I am senile, but I certainly sense the smell of Joseph.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ إِنَّكَ لَفِي ضَلَٰلِكَ ٱلۡقَدِيمِ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo tallaahi innaka lafee dalaalikal qadeem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "By Allah, indeed you are in your [same] old error."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They replied, “By Allah! You are definitely still in your old delusion.”

ayahs.textArabic: فَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَ ٱلۡبَشِيرُ أَلۡقَىٰهُ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦ فَٱرۡتَدَّ بَصِيرٗاۖ قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Falammaaa an jaaa' albasheeru alqaahu 'alaa wajhihee fartadda baseeran qaala alam aqul lakum inneee a'lamu minal laahi maa laa ta'lamoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And when the bearer of good tidings arrived, he cast it over his face, and he returned [once again] seeing. He said, "Did I not tell you that I know from Allah that which you do not know?"
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: But when the bearer of the good news arrived, he cast the shirt over Jacob’s face, so he regained his sight. Jacob then said ˹to his children˺, “Did I not tell you that I truly know from Allah what you do not know?”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالُواْ يَٰٓأَبَانَا ٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا خَٰطِـِٔينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaaloo yaaa-abaanas taghfir lanaa zunoo-banaaa innaa kunnaa khaati'een
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: They said, "O our father, ask for us forgiveness of our sins; indeed, we have been sinners."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: They begged, “O our father! Pray for the forgiveness of our sins. We have certainly been sinful.”

ayahs.textArabic: قَالَ سَوۡفَ أَسۡتَغۡفِرُ لَكُمۡ رَبِّيٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qaala sawfa astaghfiru lakum Rabbeee innahoo Huwal Ghafoorur Raheem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: He said, "I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: He said, “I will pray to my Lord for your forgiveness. He ˹alone˺ is indeed the All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

ayahs.textArabic: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُواْ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ ءَاوَىٰٓ إِلَيۡهِ أَبَوَيۡهِ وَقَالَ ٱدۡخُلُواْ مِصۡرَ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ ءَامِنِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Falammaa dakhaloo 'alaa Yoosufa aawaaa ilaihi abayaihi Wa-qaalad khuloo Misra in shaaa' al-laahu aamineen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said, "Enter Egypt, Allah willing, safe [and secure]."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: When they entered Joseph’s presence, he received his parents ˹graciously˺ and said, “Enter Egypt, Allah willing, in security.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيۡهِ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِ وَخَرُّواْ لَهُۥ سُجَّدٗاۖ وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ هَٰذَا تَأۡوِيلُ رُءۡيَٰيَ مِن قَبۡلُ قَدۡ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّي حَقّٗاۖ وَقَدۡ أَحۡسَنَ بِيٓ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَنِي مِنَ ٱلسِّجۡنِ وَجَآءَ بِكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡبَدۡوِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَن نَّزَغَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنَ إِخۡوَتِيٓۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَطِيفٞ لِّمَا يَشَآءُۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-raf'a abawaihi 'alal 'arshi Wa-kharroo lahoo sujjadaa; Wa-qaala yaaa-abati haaza taaweelu ru'yaaya min qablu qad ja'alahaa Rabbee haqqaa; Wa-qad ahsana beee iz akhrajanee minas sijni Wa-jaaa'a bikum minal badwi mim ba'di an nazaghash Shaitaanu bainee Wa-baina ikhwatee; inna Rabbee lateeful limaa yashaaa'; innahoo Huwal 'Aleemul Hakeem
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they bowed to him in prostration. And he said, "O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Then he raised his parents to the throne, and they all fell down in prostration to Joseph, who then said, “O my dear father! This is the interpretation of my old dream. My Lord has made it come true. He was truly kind to me when He freed me from prison, and brought you all from the desert after Satan had ignited rivalry between me and my siblings. Indeed my Lord is subtle in fulfilling what He wills. Surely He ˹alone˺ is the All-Knowing, All-Wise.”

ayahs.textArabic: ۞ رَبِّ قَدۡ ءَاتَيۡتَنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُلۡكِ وَعَلَّمۡتَنِي مِن تَأۡوِيلِ ٱلۡأَحَادِيثِۚ فَاطِرَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَنتَ وَلِيِّۦ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۖ تَوَفَّنِي مُسۡلِمٗا وَأَلۡحِقۡنِي بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Rabbi qad aataitanee minal mulki Wa-'allamtanee min taaweelil ahaadees; faati-ras samaawaati wal-ardi Anta waliyyee fid dunyaa wal-Aakhirati tawaffanee muslimanw Wa-alhiqnee bissaaliheen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: My Lord, You have given me [something] of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: “My Lord! You have surely granted me authority and taught me the interpretation of dreams. ˹O˺ Originator of the heavens and the earth! You are my Guardian in this world and the Hereafter. Allow me to die as one who submits and join me with the righteous.”

ayahs.textArabic: ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيۡكَۖ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيۡهِمۡ إِذۡ أَجۡمَعُوٓاْ أَمۡرَهُمۡ وَهُمۡ يَمۡكُرُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Zaalika min ambaaa'il ghaibi nooheehi ilaika Wa-maa kunta ladaihim iz ajma'ooo amrahum Wa-hum yamkuroon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal, [O Muhammad], to you. And you were not with them when they put together their plan while they conspired.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: That is from the stories of the unseen which We reveal to you ˹O Prophet˺. You were not present when they ˹all˺ made up their minds, and when they plotted ˹against Joseph˺.

ayahs.textArabic: وَمَآ أَكۡثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَوۡ حَرَصۡتَ بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-maa aksarun naasi Wa-law harasta bimu'mineen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And most of the people, although you strive [for it], are not believers.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And most people will not believe—no matter how keen you are—

ayahs.textArabic: وَمَا تَسۡـَٔلُهُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۡ أَجۡرٍۚ إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكۡرٞ لِّلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-maa tas'aluhum 'alaihi min ajr; in huwa illaa zikrul lil'aalameen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And you do not ask of them for it any payment. It is not except a reminder to the worlds.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: even though you are not asking them for a reward for this ˹Quran˺. It is only a reminder to the whole world.

ayahs.textArabic: وَكَأَيِّن مِّنۡ ءَايَةٖ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيۡهَا وَهُمۡ عَنۡهَا مُعۡرِضُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-ka-ayyim min Aayatin fis samaawaati wal-ardi yamurroona 'alaihaa Wa-hum 'anhaa mu'ridoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And how many a sign within the heavens and earth do they pass over while they, therefrom, are turning away.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: How many signs in the heavens and the earth do they pass by with indifference!

ayahs.textArabic: وَمَا يُؤۡمِنُ أَكۡثَرُهُم بِٱللَّهِ إِلَّا وَهُم مُّشۡرِكُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-maa yu'minu aksaru-hum billaahi illaa Wa-hum mushrikoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And most of them believe not in Allah except while they associate others with Him.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And most of them do not believe in Allah without associating others with Him ˹in worship˺.

ayahs.textArabic: أَفَأَمِنُوٓاْ أَن تَأۡتِيَهُمۡ غَٰشِيَةٞ مِّنۡ عَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡ تَأۡتِيَهُمُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ بَغۡتَةٗ وَهُمۡ لَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Afa-aminooo an taatiya-hum ghaashiyatum min 'azaabil laahi aw taatiyahumus Saa'atu baghtatanw Wa-hum laa yash'uroon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Then do they feel secure that there will not come to them an overwhelming [aspect] of the punishment of Allah or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Do they feel secure that an overwhelming torment from Allah will not overtake them, or that the Hour will not take them by surprise when they least expect ˹it˺?

ayahs.textArabic: قُلۡ هَٰذِهِۦ سَبِيلِيٓ أَدۡعُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۚ عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا۠ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِيۖ وَسُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Qul haazihee sabeeleee ad'ooo ilal laah; 'alaa baseera-tin ana Wa-manit taba'anee Wa-Subhaanal laahi Wa-maaa ana minal mushrikeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: Say, "This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Him."
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “This is my way. I invite to Allah with insight—I and those who follow me. Glory be to Allah, and I am not one of the polytheists.”

ayahs.textArabic: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ إِلَّا رِجَالٗا نُّوحِيٓ إِلَيۡهِم مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓۗ أَفَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَيَنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۗ وَلَدَارُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ خَيۡرٞ لِّلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Wa-maaa arsalnaa min qablika illaa rijaalan nooheee ilaihim min ahlil quraa; afalam yaseeroo fil ardi fa-yanzuroo kaifa kaana 'aaqibatul lazeena min qablihim; Wa-la-Daarul Aakhirati Khairul lillazeenat taqaw; afalaa ta'qiloon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: And We sent not before you [as messengers] except men to whom We revealed from among the people of cities. So have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? And the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear Allah; then will you not reason?
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: We only sent before you ˹O Prophet˺ men inspired by Us from among the people of each society. Have the deniers not travelled through the land to see what was the end of those ˹destroyed˺ before them? And surely the ˹eternal˺ Home of the Hereafter is far better for those mindful ˹of Allah˺. Will you not then understand?

ayahs.textArabic: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا ٱسۡتَيۡـَٔسَ ٱلرُّسُلُ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُمۡ قَدۡ كُذِبُواْ جَآءَهُمۡ نَصۡرُنَا فَنُجِّيَ مَن نَّشَآءُۖ وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأۡسُنَا عَنِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Hattaaa izas tai'asar Rusulu Wa-zannooo annahum qad kuziboo jaaa'ahum nas-runaa fanujjiya man nashaaa'u Wa-laa yuraddu baasunna 'anil qawmil mujrimeen
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: [They continued] until, when the messengers despaired and were certain that they had been denied, there came to them Our victory, and whoever We willed was saved. And Our punishment cannot be repelled from the people who are criminals.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: And when the messengers despaired and their people thought the messengers had been denied help, Our help came to them ˹at last˺. We then saved whoever We willed, and Our punishment is never averted from the wicked people.

ayahs.textArabic: لَقَدۡ كَانَ فِي قَصَصِهِمۡ عِبۡرَةٞ لِّأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِۗ مَا كَانَ حَدِيثٗا يُفۡتَرَىٰ وَلَٰكِن تَصۡدِيقَ ٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ وَتَفۡصِيلَ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ وَهُدٗى وَرَحۡمَةٗ لِّقَوۡمٖ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
ayahs.textTransliteration: Laqad kaana fee qasasihim 'ibratul li-ulil albaab; maa kaana hadeesany yuftaraa Wa-laakin tasdeeqal lazee baina yadihi Wa-tafseela kulli shai'inw Wa-hudanw Wa-rahmatal liqawmien yu'minoon
ayahs.textEnglishSaheeh: There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding. Never was the Qur'an a narration invented, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
ayahs.textEnglishMustafa: In their stories there is truly a lesson for people of reason. This message cannot be a fabrication, rather ˹it is˺ a confirmation of previous revelation, a detailed explanation of all things, a guide, and a mercy for people of faith.
